macro.reasoning: The temperature series shows a clear seasonal transition from late spring (31-34°C) to early summer with a pronounced cool/wet spell in late June (27-30°C). The last 10 days show a steady recovery from 27.7°C to 31.4°C before a rain-driven dip to 30.2°C. With the heavy precipitation event ending (9mm on final day) and humidity falling from 83% to 65%, a return to the pre-storm warming trend is expected. The 7-day forecast continues the observed ~0.3°C/day recovery rate, reaching the low-32s by day 7, consistent with the seasonal norm for early July in this regime.

micro.reasoning: Temperature shows a clear recovery trend from the June 19-21 cold/wet spell (27.7-28.6°C) back toward seasonal norms (30-34°C). Recent values (30.0-31.4°C) indicate steady warming of ~0.3-0.5°C/day as humidity drops from 83% to 59% and heavy precipitation ends. The last reading (30.2°C with 9mm rain) is a temporary rain-cooled dip; clearing conditions support continued warming.
step_reasoning: Recovery from rain-cooled 30.2°C; clearing skies and dropping humidity (65%→~60%) allow daytime heating to resume, pushing temp to ~30.5°C.
Continued drying trend (humidity ~60%→55%) and reduced cloud cover support another 0.3°C rise to ~30.8°C.
Seasonal warming momentum persists; humidity falls to ~50%, enabling stronger insolation and a 0.4°C increase to ~31.2°C.
Approaching early-June average range (31-32°C); light winds and low precipitation chances favor 0.3°C rise to ~31.5°C.
Stable high-pressure pattern likely; minimal rain and humidity ~45-50% allow further warming to ~31.8°C.
Near seasonal peak for this period; diminishing daily gains as equilibrium approached, +0.2°C to ~32.0°C.
Plateau near 32°C consistent with late-June climatology; weak cooling influences (residual moisture) balance solar heating.

synthesis.reasoning: Both macro and micro forecasts converge on the same 7-day trajectory, reflecting high confidence in a steady post-storm recovery. The macro view emphasizes the seasonal transition and ~0.3°C/day warming rate observed over the last 10 days, while the micro view details the day-by-day drivers: clearing skies, falling humidity (65%→~45%), and diminishing rain influence. The final observation (30.2°C with 9 mm rain) is a transient rain-cooled dip; with precipitation ending and humidity dropping, the underlying warming trend resumes. Uncertainty is low (±0.5°C) given the consistent pattern and agreement between scales.
